question: Cards show A, K, 4, and 7; each has a letter on one side and a number on the other. To test the rule 'if a card has a vowel on one side, it has an even number on the other', must you turn over the 4?

claims.text: You do not need to turn over the 4.
The rule is a conditional that can only be falsified by a card with a vowel on one side and an odd number on the other.
Because the rule mentions even numbers, checking the 4 may feel like a way to confirm the rule.
Every card should be checked for completeness.
Confirming instances does not test a conditional.
If the 4 has a vowel on its back, the rule holds, so this cannot falsify it.
If the 4 has a consonant on its back, the rule says nothing, since it makes no claim about consonants.
The A could hide an odd number and so must be turned.
The 7 could hide a vowel and so must be turned.
A conditional is refuted only when the antecedent is true and the consequent false, so only the A and 7 are relevant.
